about: English-side data for the grammar checker's cross-check (Phase 4): the words a line's English may contain without a Liraasa counterpart, irregular verb forms, a small synonym map for gloss drift, and the markers the literal back-translation shows. Edit here, never in code.
stopwords: a an the i me my mine myself you your yours yourself he him his she her hers it its we us our they them their this that these those there here who whom whose which what is are am was were be been being do does did have has had will would shall should can could may might must not no and or but if as so than then too very just also of to in on at by for from with into onto upon over under through about up down out off again once all any each every some such only own same both either neither nor when while where why how because since until unless although though whether let lets oh o one

lemmas._about: Irregular English forms → their base, for matching an English word against a gloss.

past._about: Irregular simple-past forms (regular pasts end in -ed). Used for the tense cross-check.
past.forms: began felt gave spoke sang made came went saw told said knew took brought thought found left held kept slept wept fell rose flew drank ate wrote taught sent lost won met heard stood sat lay led shone died became stole sold bought chose struck grew fought caught built forgot broke wore drew threw sought dreamt meant paid laid ran swam

not_past._about: Words ending in -ed that are not past-tense verbs.
not_past.forms: sacred beloved naked blessed wicked aged hundred kindred wretched rugged

participles._about: Irregular past participles, for spotting an English passive (be + participle).
participles.forms: born given spoken sung made known taken seen written told sent brought held kept lost won found heard done thought taught built left sold paid

synonyms._about: English word → other English words a gloss may use for it. Kept small: add a pair when gloss drift flags a line that is right.

markers._about: How the back-translation shows grammatical words, by Liraasa form; every other word shows the first sense of its gloss.

suffixes._about: How the back-translation shows the inflections.

same_past._about: Verbs whose past is spelled like the present (I let them leave): a line with one of these and no other tense sign has no knowable English tense.
same_past.forms: let put cut set hit cast shut spread cost hurt quit burst

pronoun_owner._about: 1.2:G27 / G32: a pronoun before de is the owner (my song), after de the owned-of object (the parent of me). The back-translation reads them so.

pronoun_object._about: A pronoun after de or after the verb.
